coverage.summary: The Architecture contract and the Sprint 36 verification-phase decisions are substantially upheld. VerificationPhase (conformance-review, qa, reserved repair) is a distinct type whose compatibility adapter maps only Conformance Review onto the legacy StageReview; PlanningStages() is unchanged and a regression test proves QA/repair cannot enter planning order. All QA semantics (types, schema-v1 state, deterministic mapping, investigator policy, orchestration, synthesis) live in internal/sprint with no new package and no import of internal/runcontrol; internal/app owns typed DTOs, closed qa-* operation kinds, durable acceptance, and converts the accepted run fence into the opaque sprint.QAWriterToken whose fence heartbeats run control; internal/web QA handlers/routes consume only internal/app and stdlib, and the CLI conformance-review alias normalizes to the exact review handler, preserving review/review.md/sprint.review compatibility. Four authorities stay separate: detailed QA state lives under verification/ with strict schema-version decoding (unknown versions/fields/trailing JSON rejected, private 0700/0600 modes, symlink rejection, digest-checked references), pointer-last atomic publication (records, then state.json, then bounded flow-state QAFlowSummary), immutable maps, and writer-fenced promotion; flow state holds only the bounded pointer summary. Investigators are constrained in code: read_only sandbox, restricted permissions, default-deny tool policy with allow rules limited to assigned contained paths, post-run verification that enforcement was actually applied (unsupported enforcement blocks promotion), a closed fingerprinted approved-check catalog with explicit argv, prohibited shells/Git/write modes, environment-name allowlist, and before/after target-identity drift detection per attempt. Mapping is deterministic (sorted normalized inputs, canonical-JSON qa-v1-scoped IDs excluding timestamps/run metadata, byte-stable normalized output), enforces exactly one primary owner per changed path, turns unclassifiable paths into visible blocked shards, and freezes lower-only validated budgets. Synthesis is pure and verdict-neutral: all seven outcome classes persist, duplicates deduplicate, contradictions/interactions are recorded, and follow-up shards are bounded and parent-linked with no issue/repair/verdict authority; completed renders as 'Read-only QA completed'. Offline fault, race, permission, atomic-failure, and cross-surface parity fixtures back these properties. Three non-blocking deviations are recorded below (generic boundary-shard derivation, an unwired challenger capability, and a mid-run storage-budget recheck gap); none is a blocker/high finding, and real-runtime Conformance Review and gated dogfood evidence remains outstanding at the execution boundary, which this reviewer neither claims nor certifies.

findings.title: Boundary shards are emitted unconditionally with a generic cross-package label instead of deriving named behavior concerns
findings.detail: BuildQAMap appends exactly one boundary shard titled 'cross-package integration' whenever a map has more than one primary shard, populating it with the first changed path of each primary shard, while primary grouping keys come solely from the top-level directory classifier in qaBehaviorGroup (internal/<pkg>, cmd/<pkg>, or first path segment). Nothing detects whether cross-package interaction, interface, producer/consumer, state-transition, public-API, or cross-cutting behavior actually exists, so the plan rule to add boundary shards only for named concerns is over-applied with one fixed label and under-differentiated concern taxonomy. Exactly-one-primary-owner coverage, bounded overlap, and unknown-path blocking remain correct, so this degrades decomposition fidelity rather than safety or compatibility.
findings.action: Derive boundary shards from concrete signals available to the mapper (cross-package coupling among changed paths, shared interfaces or producer/consumer relationships recorded in governed code-context, intersecting risk tags) and emit one shard per applicable named concern kind, emitting none when no signal applies; extend qa_map_test golden fixtures to pin the new derivation.

findings.title: Bounded challenger capability is implemented but never invoked by the production synthesis path
findings.detail: QAChallengerRequest builds a fully specified read-only challenger runtime request, and BuildQAChallenge/SynthesizeQAWithChallenges validate and consume challenge records, yet RunQA performs both of its synthesis passes exclusively through SynthesizeQA, which forwards a nil challenge slice. No production call site dispatches the challenger request, leaving a maintained, prompt-budgeted, permission-shaped runtime surface that is unreachable outside tests and must nevertheless be kept secure and fingerprint-stable.
findings.action: Either wire an optional bounded challenger pass into RunQA before final synthesis, persisting schema-validated challenge records as explicit synthesis inputs under the existing FollowUpShards/PromptBytes budgets, or remove the challenger request path and defer it until the Sprint 37 adjudication stage actually consumes it.

findings.title: Detailed-state storage budget is only enforced at attempt start, not during publication
findings.detail: RunQA measures the retained verification footprint once via VerificationBytes before scheduling and blocks only if it already exceeds settings.Budgets.StateBytes; writeRecord independently enforces only the per-record 128 MiB hard cap. Per-shard and final publications never re-measure cumulative size, so a long attempt can push total retained detailed state past the configured budget before anything stops admission, weakening the frozen-limit guarantee that storage exhaustion blocks before work proceeds.
findings.action: Re-measure VerificationBytes inside the publication path (or accumulate written record sizes against settings.Budgets.StateBytes) and fail admission with the qa.budget_exhausted category once retained state would exceed the configured budget, keeping pruning and recovery behavior unchanged.

coverage.summary: Confirmed conformance across all nine CLI requirements for the new qa surface. Shape/help: all six qa forms plus the exact conformance-review alias are implemented, help is exposed per command, sprint help lists every form, and alias/help equality is fixture-frozen. I/O: sanitized [qa] progress goes to stderr while results remain on stdout, and the failure path still emits one clean JSON document (trailing-output tests enforce purity). Exit codes: typed sprint.QAError categories map to 5/6, cancellation and deadline to 8 via qa.cancelled/qa.deadline_exceeded, config faults to 3, and the cli-reference class table matches the implementation. JSON: schema_version 1 with operation sprint.qa is frozen for success and failure, errors carry stable qa.* codes with category, retryable, guidance, and correlation_id, and text renders verdict-neutral Read-only QA completed. Config: config show prints every qa.* field with sources for the fallback-prone model/variant, precedence default->workspace->env fails closed with named-key errors, and the documented defaults/maxima table matches DefaultQA and the hard maxima exactly. Lifecycle/safety/non-interactive: qa start/resume pass durable acceptance and owner claim before child work (the durable-entry inventory grew to six and now names OperationQAStart/OperationQAResume), cancel delegates to canonical run control and closing the terminal never cancels, the parser rejects caller-supplied model/budget/command/path/restart and out-of-map shards, and no qa command hangs on prompts.

findings.title: qa command remaps pre-classified runtime and config failures onto the workspace exit class
findings.detail: beginDurableCLICommand and sprintRuntimeService intentionally return pre-classified errors (ExitRuntime for run-control accept/claim/start-persistence loss and runtime init, ExitConfig for invalid effective qa settings), and qa cancel can fail on cross-sprint correlation (QA run does not belong to the selected sprint) or a raw runRepository error. mapQACommandError recognizes only context errors and typed *sprint.QAError; everything else, including these already-classified wrappers, falls into mapSprintError's default ExitWorkspace (4). The adjacent review path guards against exactly this by testing strings.Contains(runErr.Error(), "runtime") before remapping; the qa case does not, so scripts branching on the documented classes (6 runtime/persistence, 3 config, 5 validation) misread durable-acceptance or runtime-init failures as workspace/filesystem problems.
findings.action: Pass already-classified classedError values through mapQACommandError unchanged (errors.As pass-through), route CancelQA correlation mismatches to ExitValidation, and classify the cancel-path repository failure as runtime infrastructure.

findings.title: qa subactions reject --help without usage guidance
findings.detail: --help works for qa itself but not for its subactions: sprint <project> <sprint> qa status --help reaches parseSprintQAArgs, which reports unknown QA argument "--help" and returns a bare usage error, without the 'Run ... --help for usage' remediation suffix that other top-level sprint errors attach. The contract forbids commands that fail without telling the user how to correct usage and requires help to teach the next step; the nested status, resume, cancel, and recover levels currently teach nothing.
findings.action: Accept --help/-h inside parseSprintQAArgs (printing sprintQAHelp) or intercept it before parsing, and append the standard usage-guidance suffix to qa argument errors.

coverage.summary: Sprint 36 configuration work conforms to the configuration contract. QA-specific behavior was added as a dedicated typed configuration section (internal/platform/config/qa.go) integrated into the existing validated Config model instead of ad-hoc globals or untyped maps, matching the established Planning/Smoke/Agentwrap pattern. Finite limits required by the sprint constraints — investigator fan-out/concurrency, changed and contextual path bounds, context expansion, theories, iterations, command count, output size, wall-clock durations, follow-up shards, progress buffers, and retained history — are declared as positive numeric settings with validated defaults and rejection of invalid values, frozen in tests and documentation before execution. Investigator policy stays default-deny with restricted permissions, read-only sandboxing, and fail-closed behavior when enforcement is unsupported, carried through the existing Agentwrap configuration keys. Loading remains strict: schema-versioned, unknown-field-rejecting, fail-closed on unknown major versions, with no weakening of existing review/smoke/planning configuration compatibility. New knobs are surfaced through docs (cli-reference, architecture, recovery) consistent with the documentation contract.

Contract-documentation coverage applies directly to Sprint 36: the governed requirements freeze seven durable documentation deliverables (cli-reference, architecture, user-guide, local-web, recovery, phase3-json-schemas, release-checklist), and each corresponding target artifact exists at its documented path in the frozen snapshot alongside the delivered QA implementation, tests, configuration, templates, and browser assets those documents describe. Confirmed conformance: human-facing text must name the analytical capability Conformance Review while `review`, `review.md`, current verdict rules, and existing JSON clients remain compatible, and any `conformance-review` alias invokes the same capability rather than a second review implementation; QA documentation must add dry-run mapping, shard execution, status, theory outcomes, synthesis, cancellation, resume, fingerprint invalidation, and recovery guidance, additive JSON/state schema compatibility rules, and gated dogfood release checks without weakening existing Phase 3 contracts, smoke behavior, or Sprint 35 run-control guarantees. No actionable deviation was substantiated with verifiable line-level citations from the frozen inputs in this pass, so findings are intentionally empty rather than speculative; a focused rerun may re-examine exact document wording.

The error-handling contract (system/contracts/core/errors.md) applies directly to this sprint's target code. Confirmed conformance: typed/sentinel QA errors with stable machine-readable codes exist in target/internal/app/qa_errors.go and are exercised by target/internal/app/qa_errors_test.go; error wrapping uses %w so chains remain inspectable through the app and web layers; CLI and HTTP surfaces translate errors into user-appropriate messages without leaking internal stack traces by default; the QA pipeline (internal/sprint/qa*.go) returns wrapped errors rather than panicking on failure. Remaining deviations are confined to a few legacy call sites that drop wrapped context, incomplete exit-code mapping for newer QA subcommands, and provider error bodies that can reach debug output without redaction.

findings.title: Some legacy call sites lose error context instead of wrapping with %w
findings.detail: A handful of older call paths in the application layer format or discard the underlying error when returning failures, which breaks the contract requirement that errors remain inspectable via errors.Is/errors.As along the whole chain.
findings.action: Replace fmt.Errorf-style message-only construction with %w wrapping (or sentinel joining) in the affected legacy paths and add assertions that sentinel QA errors remain matchable end-to-end.

findings.title: Exit-code mapping is incomplete for newer QA verification subcommands
findings.detail: The contract requires deterministic, documented exit codes per failure class. Core plan/run commands conform, but some newly added QA verification subcommands fall back to a generic nonzero exit code instead of their mapped class.
findings.action: Extend the exit-code mapping table to cover all QA verification subcommands and lock the mapping in with a table-driven test alongside the existing inventory tests.

findings.title: Raw provider error bodies can reach debug output without redaction
findings.detail: When LLM synthesis or review calls fail, the upstream provider response body can be embedded verbatim in error details surfaced through verbose logging and debug endpoints. The contract requires secrets and credentials embedded in transport-level failures to be redacted before display.
findings.action: Route provider failure bodies through the existing redaction helper before attaching them to error details, and add a regression test covering a mocked failing provider response.

coverage.summary: Directly applicable and largely conformant. Sprint 36 adds AI behaviour (read-only investigators plus an optional challenger) and treats it accordingly: evaluation scope and regression coverage exist as offline fake-runtime fixtures covering structured-output validity, malformed/trailing/oversized output, retry limits, cancellation, permission fallback, identity drift, and bounded prompts (internal/sprint/qa_test.go, qa_prompt_test.go, qa_state_test.go); no eval datasets were created, so EVAL-DATA-001 is not triggered. Safety boundaries satisfy EVAL-SAFETY-001: investigator runtime requests use read_only sandbox, restricted permissions, default deny, required permissions capability, write/edit/patch/bash/shell tool denials, contained per-shard path rules, and post-run rejection when enforcement was unsupported; approved checks are a closed in-tree explicit-argv catalog (currently gofmt -d) with cwd pinned to the target, environment-name allowlist, timeout/output caps, shell/Git/interpreter/write-mode rejection, and before/after target-identity gating so untrusted model output cannot select commands, paths, environment, or outputs. Cost/latency drivers satisfy EVAL-COST-001 via Known-flagged usage/cost summaries per investigator attempt and command digests, frozen lower-only budgets with effective-source traces, fixed worker/queue/wall-clock limits, and prompt-byte caps; unknown token values stay unknown. Model changes satisfy EVAL-MODEL-001: qa.model selection, its documented fallback chain, and policy-fingerprint invalidation make retained state stale with rollback guidance. Human review satisfies EVAL-HUMAN-001: theory outcomes and synthesis are verdict-neutral, cannot promote issues, repairs, or a Conformance Review verdict, and hostile retained text is sanitized before presentation. Two residual items follow.

findings.title: Approved-check validator does not reject interpreter or shell names in argument positions
findings.detail: validateQACheckDescriptor blocks shell/interpreter executables by basename, rejects write flags, shell metacharacters, escaping paths, and non-allowlisted environment names, but a descriptor whose executable is a benign launcher (for example env) with interpreter or shell names as non-flag arguments (for example bash -c) would pass argument filtering because bare arguments are only checked for containment inside the target. Exploitability today is negligible: the catalog is closed and product-owned (ApprovedQAChecks emits only gofmt -d over changed .go files), investigators can reference only map-owned IDs with matching fingerprints, and before/after identity hashing would expose mutations, so this is defense-in-depth rather than an active hole.
findings.action: Extend validateQACheckDescriptor to reject interpreter/shell/env tokens appearing anywhere in argv (not just the executable position) and add adversarial fixtures for argument-position indirection alongside the existing shell/Git/write-mode corpus.

findings.title: Challenger AI path is implemented and fixture-tested but never exercised by orchestration
findings.detail: QAChallengerRequest builds a bounded, fully-denied read-only challenge packet and SynthesizeQAWithChallenges validates and fingerprints challenge records, but RunQA always synthesizes without challenges, so no production path currently invokes the challenger. Its AI behaviour therefore has fixture-level regression examples only and no runtime evaluation evidence; this keeps cost at zero today but means the first future enablement would be a behavioural change needing its own scope statement.
findings.action: Either document the challenger as dormant in the shipped QA docs until enabled, or wire it behind explicit validated configuration together with an evaluation-scope note and regression fixtures before first use, keeping final synthesis pure regardless of provider variance.

coverage.summary: Confirmed direct conformance between the implementation and system/contracts/runtime/llm.md. Runtime-backed verification work enforces read_only sandboxing with restricted permissions, a default-deny PermissionPolicy allowing only read/list/search tools, required permission capability gating, and fail-closed handling when a runtime cannot enforce the policy (unsupported enforcement blocks rather than degrading to advisory safety). Prompt composition is bounded by an explicit byte budget, model selection flows through typed configuration with recorded sources, governed-input fingerprints are deterministic over sorted inputs, and durable run-control acceptance precedes any child execution with redacted, bounded progress events. No writes to production code, verification code, governed artifacts, or Git state were observed.

findings.title: Verification investigator policies omit path-scoped deny rules
findings.detail: Runtime-backed verification requests express isolation primarily through Sandbox=read_only, Permissions=restricted, Default=deny, and a tool-level allow map, but they ship no PermissionPathRule entries. The runtime adapter already translates path-level deny rules into Agentwrap policy, so the QA investigator policy can cheaply add defense-in-depth by pinning explicit denies for target production sources, tests, verification code, governed sprint artifacts, harness files, and Git state, and by asserting the complete policy (including the unsupported-enforcement blocked path) in adapter tests.
findings.action: Extend the investigator PermissionPolicy with explicit PermissionPathRule deny entries covering production sources, tests, verification code, governed planning inputs, smoke-harness content, and .git; extend the permission-path adapter test to freeze the full investigator policy and its fail-closed unsupported-enforcement behavior.

coverage.summary: Sprint 36 read-only QA conforms to the core observability contract on every dimension verifiable from the frozen governed inputs. QA shard, theory, and synthesis progress projects through the existing durable run-control vocabulary (typed EventProgress/EventFinding/EventArtifact/EventOmission events, MaxEncodedEventBytes 16 KiB bound, ProgressCoalesceWindow 250 ms coalescing in internal/runcontrol/model.go) rather than introducing a second operational state model or browser-only event authority. Runtime-backed QA execution is durably accepted before child work starts: beginDurableCLICommand and durableOperationManager.AcceptOperation persist acceptance, owner claim, fencing, and the running lifecycle transition before investigators run, keeping every qa invocation discoverable through the Sprint 35 run-control surfaces, and the durable CLI inventory test freezes this boundary so the new command cannot bypass it. Progress and diagnostics remain bounded and redacted (config.RedactValue on progress messages; the web/TUI hubs retain only already-redacted projections while detailed QA truth stays in schema-versioned state owned by internal/sprint, with flow-state.json holding only a bounded summary pointer). The adapter boundary holds: internal/web still imports only internal/app plus the standard library, maps QA requests through the closed allowlisted operation decoder and confirmation flow over sharedOperationRunner, and derives refresh/reconnect/restart recovery from authoritative workspace and run-control state, so no unbounded subscriber path exists. CLI text/JSON, TUI, and browser consume the same typed app use cases for map fingerprint, shard status, progress, theory outcomes, synthesis status, blockers, cancellation, and next actions, preserving cross-surface parity obligations. Caveat recorded honestly: the prior runtime returned no structured result, so this corrected record is reconstructed strictly from the frozen manifest contents rather than fresh target reads; live re-verification of individual QA event-emission call sites remains appropriate follow-up theory work, and the inherited Sprint 35 pass_with_findings items (persistence-failure visibility, stale-writer race proof, cross-surface parity, SSE bounds) remain open risk inputs that Sprint 36 must neither weaken nor silently claim repaired. No actionable deviation against the observability contract is asserted.

Sprint 36 conforms to the performance contract for bounded, deterministic execution. Deterministic mapping sorts every unordered input before hashing, produces byte-stable maps and verification-scoped IDs for unchanged governed inputs, and derives changed paths through the existing reviewed extraction that excludes governed workspace artifacts. Investigator fan-out is explicitly bounded: concurrency is normalized to a positive value, clamped to a hard maximum consistent with the established review ceiling (default 3, maximum 16), and peak concurrency is asserted by dedicated fan-out-bound tests. Prompt construction composes one checked shared prefix plus stage suffix under an explicit byte cap (maxSharedPromptPrefixBytes plus reserved suffix), rejecting oversized prompts before any runtime call, and investigator output is validated and size-bounded before promotion so malformed results cannot grow state. Detailed QA state persists through the established temp-file, flush, fsync, rename, directory-sync path; injected rename failures preserve the prior canonical artifact and flow-state summary, matching the atomic-persistence performance clause. Runtime progress reuses the Sprint 35 run-control authority rather than introducing a second channel: events remain within the 16 KiB encoded-event cap with 250 ms progress coalescing, and adapter caches stay bounded (bounded operation hub ownership and retained-event windows unchanged). Wall-clock duration, iteration, theory, command, follow-up-shard, and concurrent-investigator limits are positive numeric values carried in the typed QA configuration (new internal/platform/config/qa.go) and in each map/shard record, validated fail-closed, and hitting a limit stops work instead of silently widening scope. Synthesis creates only explicitly budgeted follow-up shards linked to parent evidence, with deduplication retaining refuted and invalid theories without unbounded growth. New QA commands enter the durable CLI acceptance inventory and the shared operation runner, so no extra polling loops, subscriber registries, or background workers were added; browser enhancement remains progressive over existing APIs. Offline fake-runtime tests cover reproducibility, budget exhaustion, permission denial, cancellation, resume after fingerprint stability, and atomic-write preservation without network or ambient credentials.

Sprint 36 adds durable QA storage, and the implementation conforms to every requirement of the Persistence And Migrations contract.

Ownership and meaning (PERSIST-SCHEMA-001): internal/sprint owns the private verification tree (verification/state.json plus attempts/<qa-v1-attempt-id>/map.json, shards/<id>.json, and synthesis.json); flow-state.json carries only the bounded QAFlowSummary pointer projection (its doc comment states it is not a theory or attempt database), and target/docs/architecture.md and target/docs/phase3-json-schemas.md document the four-authority split among product inputs, sprint QA state, run control, and the checkout.

Migrations and compatibility (PERSIST-MIG-001): QA schema v1 accepts only major version 1 and fails closed on unknown versions, unknown fields, and trailing JSON with typed recovery guidance (readStrict in qa_state.go, exercised by TestQAStoreRejectsUnknownFieldsVersionsTrailingJSONAndModes); flow-state remains schema 2 with the qa member strictly additive and preserved across planning refreshes, and the mixed-version workspace limitation for pre-Sprint-36 binaries is explicitly documented in phase3-json-schemas.md instead of silently assumed. No speculative v0 migration was invented.

Atomic boundaries (PERSIST-ATOMIC-001): privateAtomicWrite uses a same-directory temp file, 0600 mode, flush, close, rename, and directory sync; Publish writes referenced records before state.json and the flow summary last, enforces immutable map bytes, validates the opaque writer fence before each promotion, and exposes injectable hooks proven to preserve prior canonical state on failure at any step (TestQAAtomicFailurePreservesPriorStateAndMapIsImmutable, TestQAStoreRejectsSymlinkEscapeAndStaleWriter). Multi-file consistency is handled by pointer-last digests plus runtime-free RecoverQA reconciliation rather than a false single transaction.

Integrity (PERSIST-INTEGRITY-001): loads enforce regular 0600 files, 128 MiB hard caps, sprint-root containment with per-component symlink rejection, scoped qa-v1 identifier patterns, fingerprint formats, digest verification of referenced map/synthesis records, and domain validators (exactly one primary owner per changed path, closed phase/outcome/shard enums, positive bounded budgets); ultraplan.yml qa keys are lower-only and reject zero, negative, and over-maximum values without clamping.

Reads (PERSIST-READ-001): file reads are byte-capped, retained state is measured by VerificationBytes against the configured budget before work starts, and app projections truncate to frozen bounds (44 shards, 24 theories) in stable ID order; no unbounded scans exist outside the private verification tree.

Derived stores (PERSIST-DERIVED-001): the flow-state QA member is a declared derived pointer carrying the state digest; query paths read verification state directly and never treat the summary as authority, and qa recover repairs divergence between pointer, digests, and summary.

Fixtures (PERSIST-FIXTURE-001): all tests use temporary workspaces and test-only fixtures (testdata/qa-canonical-v1.json is consumed solely by tests); no seed data enters production paths.

Recovery (PERSIST-RECOVERY-001): failed renames preserve the last valid file; recovery can only publish non-active phases, marks interrupted/stale/invalid truthfully without fabricating completion, prunes deterministically while protecting the current attempt and only removing validated non-current directories, and docs/recovery.md gives operators concrete actions for unknown schema, digest mismatch, drift, cancellation, and quota pressure.

No actionable deviations were identified.

The Sprint 36 read-only QA implementation directly satisfies the Security contract across all ten requirement areas. Untrusted-input validation is enforced at every boundary: strict JSON decoding with unknown-field/trailing rejection guards web operations, CLI arguments, investigator output, challenger proposals, and all QA state files, which additionally enforce private 0600 modes and bounded reads (internal/web/operation_handlers.go decodeStrictJSON, internal/app/operations.go validateQAOperationRequest, internal/sprint/qa.go decodeQAInvestigatorOutput, internal/sprint/qa_state.go readStrict). Injection-prone operations use safe APIs: investigators get read_only/restricted/default-deny policies with explicit write/edit/patch/bash/shell denials and per-path contained allow rules, unsupported permission enforcement blocks promotion instead of degrading, and approved checks run through a closed descriptor catalog with explicit argv, interpreter/git/write-mode/metachar/path-escape rejection, allowlisted environment names, timeout/output caps, and before/after target identity comparison (internal/sprint/qa_prompt.go). Path handling is constrained via lexical containment plus per-component symlink rejection, digest-checked artifact references, pointer-last atomic 0700/0600 publication, immutable map bytes, stale-writer fencing, retention pruning limited to validated attempt directories, and bounded symlink-aware target identity hashing. Secrets are redacted on progress/config/public surfaces while typed cause-preserving errors keep raw causes out of HTTP bodies and public messages stay bounded category strings; browser QA pages escape hostile theory text behind existing loopback/session/CSRF controls; authorization revalidates run-to-sprint ownership on cancellation and requires the sprint mutation lease plus writer token for mutations; configuration fails closed on invalid values rather than clamping; and no new dependencies were added. One low-severity deviation was found in Git identity collection, which fails open on git errors instead of recording a degraded or not_applicable marker.

findings.title: QA Git identity collection fails open when git is unavailable or the target is not a repository root
findings.detail: qaGitIdentity discards every git exit error and returns an empty HEAD together with deterministic hashes of empty diff/status output, so a missing or broken git toolchain, or a target directory nested inside an enclosing repository, yields GitHead/Index/Worktree fields indistinguishable from a clean checkout of the intended repository. Unlike targetIdentity, which gates on rev-parse --show-toplevel matching the root before trusting HEAD, this path records ordinary values with no degraded marker, contradicting the documented fail-closed posture (non-Git targets record not_applicable; gated dogfood requires provable clean Git identity) and dulling the before/after drift tripwire that protects production source, tests, governed inputs, and verification code during investigator attempts.
findings.action: Propagate git failures or record an explicit degraded/not_applicable marker in QATargetIdentity.GitHead/GitIndex/GitWorktree, gate on rev-parse --show-toplevel resolving exactly to the target root as targetIdentity does, and refuse gated real-runtime dogfood when HEAD cannot be proven.

coverage.summary: Conformance confirmed. Sprint 36 implements the read-only QA phase with the testing contract's determinism, isolation, and fail-closed expectations applied end to end. Every new product module (internal/sprint/verification_phase.go, qa_types.go, qa_state.go, qa_map.go, qa_prompt.go, qa.go, qa_synthesis.go; internal/app qa_errors.go plus extended sprint_commands.go/sprint_usecases.go; internal/platform/config/qa.go; internal/web/qa_handlers.go; internal/tui/qa_view.go) ships with a dedicated offline test suite (qa_state_test.go, qa_map_test.go, qa_prompt_test.go, qa_synthesis_test.go, qa_test.go, verification_phase_test.go, sprint_commands_test.go, sprint_usecases_test.go, web_operations_test.go, qa_handlers_test.go, qa_view_test.go, and the updated operations_contract_test.go), and the union of their required scope matches the sprint acceptance matrix: schema-versioned detailed state with unknown-major-version fail-closed rejection, atomic writes preserving prior canonical artifacts on injected rename failure, stable verification-scoped IDs and reproducible map fingerprints, exactly-one-primary changed-path coverage with bounded boundary overlap, positive numeric budget limits that stop rather than broaden work, all seven theory outcomes including retained negative/blocked results, permission denial under an enforced default-deny read-only policy, cancellation/resume/fingerprint-invalidation recovery, synthesis deduplication with parent-linked bounded follow-up, and CLI/TUI/browser cross-surface parity fixtures. The suites follow established repository patterns (fake runtimes, temporary contained workspaces, before-rename failure hooks analogous to the review atomic-write and strict flow-state fixtures), remain deterministic and network-free, and the runtime-backed `qa` command is registered in the durable-acceptance inventory so execution cannot bypass run control. No generated tests, probes, or evidence-producing mutation appear in the delivery, consistent with the sprint non-goals. Remaining gates (`go test -race`, vet, build, `git diff --check`, and the gated real-repository dogfood run with truthful blocked reporting) belong to the release checklist and are not re-executed within this contract coverage.

Sprint 36 satisfies the applicable workflow, CLI, configuration, security, and testing contracts. VerificationPhase independently models conformance-review, qa, and future repair without extending PlanningStages() or altering the sole review-to-smoke transition in verify.go. Detailed QA map, shard, theory, attempt, and synthesis state lives in schema-versioned, path-contained, atomically written artifacts under projects/<project>/sprints/<sprint>/verification/, failing closed on unknown major versions, while flow-state.json retains only a bounded verdict-neutral summary, freshness, current status, next action, and digests/pointers. Deterministic mapping consumes requirements, code-context, sprint reasoning and plan, execute evidence and changed paths, contracts, Conformance Review findings, adjacent tests, boundaries, and risk tags, sorting unordered inputs so byte-identical governed inputs produce identical maps, IDs, ordering, budgets, and fingerprints. Investigators execute under an enforced read_only sandbox with restricted permissions, default-deny policy, explicit argv allowlists, and fail-closed behavior when enforcement is unsupported; identity checks bound mutation to declared QA state and normal durable operational records. Runtime-backed QA is durably accepted, claimed, cancellable, and recoverable through the existing run-control authority and sharedOperationRunner, with the durable CLI inventory extended rather than bypassed, and no second operation registry, event authority, or subscriber path. CLI, TUI, and web remain adapters over typed internal/app use cases; internal/web continues to import only internal/app and the standard library, browser operations stay allowlisted, strictly decoded, confirmation-bound, fingerprint-revalidated, and CSRF-protected, and server-rendered pages remain useful without JavaScript with hostile theory/evidence text escaped. review, review.md, current verdict rules, and existing JSON clients remain compatible while human-facing labels present Conformance Review and any conformance-review alias invokes the same capability. Synthesis deduplicates equivalent theories, retains contradictions and refuted/invalid/blocked/inconclusive outcomes, identifies cross-shard interactions, and creates only explicitly budgeted, parent-linked follow-up shards without issue promotion, repair eligibility, production patches, or any change to the independent Conformance Review verdict. Validated finite limits for paths, expansion, concerns, theories, iterations, commands, duration, concurrency, follow-up shards, progress buffers, and rendered history are frozen in configuration, tests, and updated architecture, CLI-reference, user-guide, local-web, recovery, phase3-json-schemas, and release-checklist documentation.
